title: Instruction List: arithmetic, comparison and a jump on a rising edge
summary: Keep a running total in an INT variable, add to it on each press with ADD and a conditional jump, and turn it into three BOOL results with LT, EQ and GT.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence with one 10 ms task; they do not establish the range of a real sensor or the overflow behaviour of a particular controller, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Use ADD on a number in the current result, and LT, EQ and GT to turn a number into a BOOL.
Skip a group of lines with JMPCN so that a number changes only on the rising edge of an input.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/TypedSteps.il the three comparisons at the end are written: LD Total loads the INT, LT 10 compares it and leaves a BOOL, and ST Low stores it. Write the arithmetic above them: on each rising edge of Step (Step ON now and StepWas OFF) add 5 to Total, with LD Total, ADD 5, ST Total; JMPCN skip jumps over those lines when the condition is FALSE. Then, while Reset is TRUE, load 0 and store it in Total.
stages.checkpoint: Total goes 0, 5, 10, 15, and the three outputs show which band it is in.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Step is pressed three times, the first press lasting two scans. Predict which output is ON at {{t:20}}, {{t:40}} and {{t:60}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:TypedSteps.Low=true,TypedSteps.Exact=false,TypedSteps.High=false@20|Low}} at {{t:20}} ms (Total is 5); {{v:TypedSteps.Low=false,TypedSteps.Exact=true,TypedSteps.High=false@40|Exact}} at {{t:40}} ms (Total is 10); {{v:TypedSteps.Low=false,TypedSteps.Exact=false,TypedSteps.High=true@60|High}} at {{t:60}} ms (Total is 15).

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press Check: The starting program remembers Step in StepWas and writes the three comparisons, but never changes Total, so Low stays ON for ever; add 5 to Total on each rising edge of Step and clear it while Reset is TRUE.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named TypedSteps and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:20}}, {{t:40}} and {{t:60}} ms: exactly one of the three outputs is ON each time, and Reset at {{t:80}} ms brings Low back.
stages.checkpoint: Exact is ON only at the one total of 10, from {{t:40}} ms; the long first press added 5 once, not twice.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: What happens if you write Exact with GE 10? And if you remove ANDN StepWas? Try each and see which assertion fails.
stages.checkpoint: A comparison leaves a BOOL in the current result, and EQ is not the same as GE. Without ANDN StepWas a press that lasts two scans adds twice. The scenario only watches the three BOOL outputs; it does not show the value of Total itself or what happens when an INT overflows.

hints.text: Total is an INT, so LD Total, ADD 5 and ST Total keep it an INT. A rising edge is LD Step followed by ANDN StepWas. JMPCN skip jumps to the label skip: when the current result is FALSE.
LD Step, ANDN StepWas, JMPCN skip, LD Total, ADD 5, ST Total, skip:, then the lines that copy Step to StepWas, then LD Reset, JMPCN keep, LD 0, ST Total, keep:, before the three comparisons.

faultCases: The starting program remembers Step in StepWas and writes the three comparisons, but never changes Total, so Low stays ON for ever; add 5 to Total on each rising edge of Step and clear it while Reset is TRUE.
